note: Realistic filled-in states in the scoring engine's shape. `expected` is computed by `bin/test-personas --update` and verified by `bin/test-personas`. Background diabetic retinopathy (R1) is deliberately NOT 'referable' per NHS Diabetic Eye Screening Programme criteria (only pre-proliferative/proliferative/maculopathy are), so it grades minor severity, not major — the second persona below isolates exactly that distinction.

personas.name: normal-fundus-examination-complete
personas.description: A normal routine fundus examination: healthy optic discs, normal macula and periphery, no diabetic retinopathy, every mandatory report section present — expect normal classification + none severity + 100% completeness + routine follow-up + no-action.

state.clinicalHistory: Routine eye health check, no visual symptoms.
state.findingsNarrative: Optic discs healthy, normal cup-to-disc ratio bilaterally. Macula and retinal periphery normal. No diabetic retinopathy.
state.impression: Normal eye examination; no ophthalmic pathology identified.
state.recommendedFollowUp: No further ophthalmic follow-up required for this indication.

expected.recommendedAction: No specific eye-care follow-up required; manage per usual care.

firedRules.description: No abnormal structured findings on an interpretable examination; classified as normal.
No abnormal finding; abnormality severity graded none.
No escalation rule fired; routine follow-up only.

personas.name: abnormal-background-diabetic-retinopathy-minor-complete
personas.description: Annual diabetic eye screening finds scattered microaneurysms and dot-blot haemorrhages, consistent with background diabetic retinopathy (R1): this grade is deliberately not 'referable' (only pre-proliferative, proliferative, or maculopathy are), so it grades minor severity rather than major; report complete — expect abnormal classification + minor severity (reportingCategory R1) + 100% completeness + recommended follow-up (routine monitoring within 3 months).

state.clinicalHistory: Annual diabetic eye screening, type 2 diabetes.
state.findingsNarrative: Scattered microaneurysms and a few dot-blot haemorrhages in both retinas, consistent with background diabetic retinopathy. No maculopathy, no pre-proliferative or proliferative changes.
state.impression: Background diabetic retinopathy (R1) bilaterally; no referable features.
state.recommendedFollowUp: Continue annual diabetic eye screening; no referral required for background retinopathy alone.

expected.recommendedAction: Recommend routine monitoring of the minor finding per the relevant pathway.

firedRules.description: One or more abnormal structured findings are present; classified as abnormal.
A minor structured abnormal finding (e.g. reduced acuity, unilateral field defect, or background retinopathy) is present; abnormality severity graded minor.

personas.name: critical-acute-angle-closure-glaucoma-uncommunicated-incomplete
personas.description: Acutely painful red right eye with a fixed, mid-dilated pupil and an intraocular pressure of 52 mmHg (above the 40 mmHg acute threshold): this auto-escalates classification to critical and follow-up to critical-alert regardless of the other axes, with the recommended action naming a same-day ophthalmology review; the result has not yet been recorded as communicated, and the clinical history, impression, and recommended follow-up sections are not yet completed while treatment is arranged — expect critical classification + major severity + 40% completeness + critical-alert follow-up + urgent-review.

state.findingsNarrative: Acutely painful red right eye with a fixed, mid-dilated pupil and a hazy cornea; intraocular pressure acutely raised at 52 mmHg, consistent with acute angle-closure glaucoma.
state.clinicianNotes: Phoned through to the on-call ophthalmology team immediately; urgent IOP-lowering treatment being arranged.

expected.recommendedAction: Arrange urgent (same-day) ophthalmology review; communicate the critical result directly to the referrer now and document the conversation.

firedRules.description: A critical ophthalmic finding (proliferative retinopathy, acutely raised IOP, or reduced acuity with optic-disc abnormality) is present; classified as critical.
Critical finding present; abnormality severity graded major.
Mandatory report section missing: clinical history.
Mandatory report section missing: recommended follow-up.
Critical ophthalmic finding auto-escalates follow-up urgency to critical-alert regardless of the other axes.

flags.description: A critical ophthalmic finding (proliferative retinopathy, acutely raised IOP, or reduced acuity with optic-disc abnormality) is present.
flags.suggestedAction: Arrange urgent ophthalmology review and communicate the critical result to the referrer immediately, documenting the communication.

flags.description: Critical finding present but the result has not been recorded as communicated.
flags.suggestedAction: Contact the referrer now and record who was informed, with date and time.

flags.description: No impression / conclusion has been recorded.
flags.suggestedAction: Add an impression that answers the clinical question.
